1.name: Valve body
1.note: Carries the water from inlet to outlet past the DN13 main seat. The diaphragm closes on that seat.

2.name: Diaphragm
2.note: The main valve. Water pressure above it holds it on the seat; when that pressure drains away, the inlet pressure lifts it. Its Ø0.8 bleed lets the chamber refill.

3.name: Pilot sleeve
3.note: Carries the Ø1.6 pilot orifice, which drains the chamber above the diaphragm when the plunger lifts. It drains faster than the bleed refills it.

4.name: Support washer
4.note: Backs the centre of the diaphragm round the pilot sleeve, so the pressure does not push it through.

5.name: Bleed bush
5.note: The Ø0.8 bleed through the diaphragm. It lets inlet water into the chamber above, and its slow refill sets the closing time.

6.name: Cover
6.note: Clamps the diaphragm rim and closes the chamber above it. That chamber is where the pilot pressure acts.

7.name: Cap screw
7.note: Four screws that hold the cover down on the body and the diaphragm.

8.name: O-ring
8.note: Seals the tube base to the cover, so water cannot leak up round the armature tube.

9.name: Tube base
9.note: Screws into the cover and holds the armature tube above the pilot.

10.name: Armature tube
10.note: A thin non-magnetic tube that holds the water in and guides the plunger. The magnetic flux crosses its wall.

11.name: Pole piece
11.note: The fixed magnetic core at the top of the tube. The plunger is pulled up to it, closing the air gap.

12.name: Plunger
12.note: The moving core. The coil pulls it up 3.2 mm, a small stroke that is the only mechanical movement of the signal.

13.name: Pilot seal
13.note: Soft face at the foot of the plunger. It shuts the Ø1.6 pilot when the coil is off, and the pilot pressure helps hold it there.

14.name: Plunger spring
14.note: Pushes the plunger down onto the pilot when the coil is off, so the valve is normally closed.

15.name: Coil bobbin
15.note: The former the winding is wound on, and it insulates the wire from the tube.

16.name: Winding
16.note: The 24 V DC coil, about 10 W. Its current makes the flux that pulls the plunger in.

17.name: Yoke frame
17.note: A steel strap that returns the flux round the outside of the coil, so it is not lost to the air.

18.name: Yoke plate
18.note: Closes the magnetic circuit at the bottom of the coil. The flux crosses the tube wall into the plunger here.

19.name: Coil housing
19.note: A moulded shell that encapsulates the coil and yoke, and carries the connector.

20.name: Washer
20.note: Spreads the clamping load of the nut on the coil housing.

21.name: Hex nut
21.note: Threads on the pole piece stud and clamps the coil assembly onto the tube.
